blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: The first object is a Deployment, the app to scale. It comes from the apps/v1 API.
blocks.why: A HorizontalPodAutoscaler, added later in the file, changes how many Pods it runs.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create first: the Deployment to scale

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: The autoscaler finds the Deployment by this name.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: The name the autoscaler looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app

blocks.title: No replicas field
blocks.what: The selector manages Pods labelled app: busy-app. There is no replicas line.
blocks.why: The autoscaler sets replicas. Leaving it out stops kubectl apply from undoing its changes.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because apps/v1 Deployments must have a selector.
blocks.comment: Manage Pods labelled app: busy-app. The autoscaler sets the count.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app

blocks.title: Describe the Pods
blocks.what: The template is the blueprint for each Pod. It gives each Pod the selector’s label.
blocks.why: New Pods the autoscaler adds come from this blueprint.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment would have nothing to create, so Kubernetes rejects it.
blocks.comment: The blueprint for each Pod, with the label the selector looks for
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app

blocks.title: An app you can make busy
blocks.what: The container idles until a file called /tmp/busy exists. Then it uses all the CPU it may.
blocks.why: It stands in for an app under heavy load, without needing real traffic.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the Deployment, because its Pods would have nothing to run.
blocks.comment: Idle, until /tmp/busy exists. Then use as much CPU as allowed.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]

blocks.title: Requests make scaling possible
blocks.what: Each container requests 50m CPU and may use up to 100m.
blocks.why: The autoscaler measures CPU as a percentage of the request. Without a request, it cannot compute one.
blocks.ifRemoved: The autoscaler reports unknown CPU use and never scales.
blocks.comment: Request 50m CPU. The autoscaler compares use with this.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m

blocks.title: Add the autoscaler
blocks.what: Three dashes start a second object: a HorizontalPodAutoscaler, from autoscaling/v2.
blocks.why: kubectl autoscale deployment busy-app --cpu=50% --min=1 --max=3 is a shortcut that creates the same object.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Deployment always runs one Pod.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: busy-app

blocks.title: What to scale
blocks.what: scaleTargetRef names the Deployment to scale: busy-app, from apps/v1.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the autoscaler, because it must say what to scale.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: busy-app

blocks.title: Measure CPU
blocks.what: The autoscaler watches the cpu of the Pods, a Resource metric.
blocks.why: metrics-server collects these numbers. K3s includes it; EKS needs the metrics-server add-on.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes uses the default: CPU, aiming for 80% of the request.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: busy-app
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu

blocks.title: The target
blocks.what: Aim for 50% average use: 25m of each Pod’s 50m request.
blocks.why: Above the target, the autoscaler adds Pods. Below it, the autoscaler removes Pods.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the autoscaler, because a utilization target needs a number.
blocks.comment: Keep average CPU near 50% of the request
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: busy-app
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 50

blocks.title: The limits
blocks.what: Run at least 1 Pod and at most 3. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: A maximum stops a runaway app from filling the cluster.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the autoscaler, because maxReplicas is required.
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: busy-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: busy-app
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: app
          image: busybox:1.37.0
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do if [ -f /tmp/busy ]; then :; else sleep 1; fi; done"]
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 50m
            limits:
              cpu: 100m
---
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: busy-app
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: busy-app
  minReplicas: 1
  maxReplicas: 3
  metrics:
    - type: Resource
      resource:
        name: cpu
        target:
          type: Utilization
          averageUtilization: 50

notes.---: Three dashes separate objects. One file can hold several objects.
notes.apiVersion: The API group and version. Deployments are in apps/v1. Autoscalers are in autoscaling/v2.
notes.Deployment:kind: The type of object to create. A Deployment keeps identical Pods running.
notes.HorizontalPodAutoscaler:kind: The type of object to create. It changes a Deployment’s replicas to match load.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.Deployment:metadata.name: The Deployment’s name. The autoscaler’s scaleTargetRef uses it.
notes.HorizontalPodAutoscaler:metadata.name: The autoscaler’s name, used with kubectl get hpa.
notes.Deployment:spec: The desired state of the Deployment. There is no replicas line: the autoscaler sets it.
notes.HorizontalPodAutoscaler:spec: The desired state: what to scale, between which counts, and on which measure.
notes.spec.selector: Which Pods this Deployment manages. It cannot change after creation.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels: Pods must have all of these labels to be managed by this Deployment.
notes.spec.selector.matchLabels.app: Match Pods whose app label is busy-app.
notes.spec.template: The Pod template: the blueprint for every Pod this Deployment creates.
notes.spec.template.metadata: Details given to every Pod created from the template.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels: Labels given to every Pod. They must match the selector.
notes.spec.template.metadata.labels.app: Every Pod gets the label app: busy-app, so the selector finds it.
notes.spec.template.spec: What each Pod runs. This is the same spec as in a Pod file.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers: The containers in each Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. It must be unique within the Pod.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].image: A tiny image with basic shell tools, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].command: Sleep in a loop. Once /tmp/busy exists, loop without sleeping, using all allowed CPU.
notes.spec.template.spec.containers[].resource: The CPU this container asks for and may use.
What the container is guaranteed. The autoscaler measures use against it.
50m: five hundredths of a CPU core.
The most the container may use.
100m: twice the request, so a busy Pod shows 200%.
notes.spec.scaleTargetRef.name: The target’s name. It must match the Deployment exactly.
notes.spec.maxReplicas: Never more than 3 Pods, however busy.
notes.spec.metrics: What to measure. Each list item is one measure.
notes.spec.metrics[].type: Resource: a container resource such as CPU or memory, from metrics-server.
notes.spec.metrics[].resource: Which resource, and what to aim for.
notes.spec.metrics[].resource.name: cpu: measure CPU use.
notes.spec.metrics[].resource.target.type: Utilization: a percentage of each Pod’s request.
notes.spec.metrics[].resource.target.averageUt: Aim for 50% on average across the Pods.

tryIt.result: TARGETS shows cpu: <unknown>/50% for about a minute, then a low number such as 6%. REPLICAS is 1.
Prints nothing. The container now uses its full 100m CPU limit.
Within about a minute, cpu climbs to around 200% and REPLICAS rises to 3, the maximum.
Events show New size: 3, because CPU use was above the target.

expect: New size: 3; reason: cpu resource utilization (percentage of request) above target

tryIt.result: Removes the Deployment and the autoscaler. Left running, it would wait 5 minutes before scaling down.

questions.question: A Pod uses 25m CPU. What utilization does the autoscaler see?
questions.explain: Utilization is use divided by the request: 25m of 50m is 50%.

questions.question: Why does the Deployment have no replicas line?
answers: The autoscaler sets the count. A replicas line would reset it on every apply.
questions.explain: The Kubernetes docs advise leaving replicas out once an autoscaler manages a Deployment.

questions.question: The app stays very busy. How many Pods can run?
answers: As many as the cluster fits
questions.explain: maxReplicas caps the count, however high the CPU use climbs.

fix.message: the HPA controller was unable to get the target's current scale: deployments.apps "busy-ap" not found
fix.explain: scaleTargetRef names busy-ap, which does not exist. The autoscaler has nothing to scale.
fix.fix: Match the Deployment’s name exactly: busy-app.
